column6: Worked: single-user 1 bit, sum 0.5*log2(7)=1.404, SIC corner R1=0.5*log2(1.75)=0.404, TDMA sum 1. Older text (not fixed): Q2 short-answer says the general BC capacity region was established via Marton; it is still open (Marton is an inner bound).

Bullet 2 overstated absolute: "for two users the region is a pentagon" holds for the Gaussian MAC or a fixed input distribution, not every MAC (general region is a convex hull of pentagons; some channels give a rectangle). Qualified to "generally" + Gaussian MAC.

Worked: rho=[[3/4,1/4],[1/4,1/4]], eigenvalues 0.854/0.146, S=0.601 bits; Bell state S(AB)=0, S(A)=1. Older text (not fixed): Q3 answer and Explainer item 2 say C_Q can be positive when C=0 (impossible, C>=C_Q; superactivation concerns two zero-Q channels); Q1 explanation calls the maximally mixed state an "equal superposition" (that is a pure state); Q4 stem grammar garbled.
Bullet 1 dropped qualifier: "non-orthogonal states give S smaller than H(p)" holds only for mixtures of pure states (mixtures of mixed states can have S > H(p)). Added "pure".

Worked BA by hand: fixed point q(1)=0.125, D=0.1, map contraction ~0.56/step so a few dozen rounds suffice; R=H(0.2)-H(0.1)=0.253. Older text (not fixed): Q1 answer option has sign error exp(+beta d); Q4 (helper/remote coding) is garbled; Explainer says Wyner-Ziv rate is R(D|Y) in general (only Gaussian has no loss) and Slepian-Wolf sum rate needs "decoders to coordinate".
Bullet 4: said the joint distribution of X and Y fixes the KL distortion, but p(y|t) depends on the encoder. Reworded to say Y defines it and no separate measure is chosen.
Worked: H(0.11)=0.4999, naive half-send scheme distortion 0.5*0.5=0.25. Older text (not fixed): Explainer says each extra bit halves the distortion; it divides it by 4 (6 dB).
Worked: expected questions 1.75 = H; uniform 4 needs 2.

H(X,Y)=H(X|Y)+H(Y|X)+I(X;Y) checked; Wyner-Ziv Gaussian no-loss correct.
